claims.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
claims.body: On the power play, New Jersey is one of the league’s best, but Calgary is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Flames take could cost them. These two rarely give each other power plays, so special teams may not get much of a say.

Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, up from 2% last season.
Anthony Mantha is on long-term injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 5 games.

NJD.head: A big edge for the Devils
NJD.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames’ best way in is keeping dangerous shots away.

CGY.head: The Flames have their work cut out
CGY.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Flames can start with keeping dangerous shots away, plus Dustin Wolf stealing the show.

story.head: Nemec returns to New Jersey
paras: The Flames (10-12-1) lost 4-1 to Minnesota on Nov 19, and the Devils (15-7-0) lost 3-2 to Montréal on Nov 18. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth).

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so the Devils’ power play bites, but theirs doesn’t. Calgary has scored 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Devils, they rarely throw hits (2nd lowest), draw more penalties than they take (3rd) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). Something has to give when the Flames’ shooting runs into the Devils’ defense.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 23 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jesper Bratt (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.
Dustin Wolf (5-6-1 / .877 SV% in 12 GS) is in line to start for Calgary. Connor Hellebuyck (7-1-0 / .913 SV% in 8 GS) has been terrific for New Jersey and will likely start.
The Devils usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.
